newsitem.title: USA: Muni buysider sees possible tax reform ahead.
newsitem.headline: Muni buysider sees possible tax reform ahead.

text.p: Loews Corporation's Mark Muller's long-term municipal market outlook includes "significant" tax reform, including grandfathered tax-exempts and newer taxable municipals, he told a group of New York area municipal professionals.

"I think this will lead to wider distribution including taxable pension funds and international investment accounts," Muller, a speaker at the Municipal Forum of New York's annual Buyers Panel here on Thursday, said.
Muller, a Loews senior vice president, envisions "a new market with a new learning process and a new set of returns not found currently in our mature and somewhat declining market."
Looking ahead, Muller said it can be argued that supply will decrease given that health care and electric utility issuers have "practically expired as tax-exempt issuers."

In 1995, the two sectors issued 40 percent less than in 1986, he said, adding that over just the past five years issuance has declined by 25 percent. The sectors currently comprise 11 percent of annual issuance, compared to 20 percent 10-years ago, he said.
Muller sees no other "significant increase" for any of the remaining sectors, except possibly transportation, he said.

On the demand side, while individual retail and property and casualty insurance company purchases currently reflect strength, flows into bond funds, which have been the "most robust engine" in the recent past, have been weak.
"Any tax reform like capital gains tax cuts or corporate de minimis tax reform we believe will diminish demand further," he said.
Tax reform could be a consequence of the medicare insolvency debate for the year 2000, and the attention it will receive in 1998, Muller said.
